descriptionChirho: A female royal ruler or consort, used predominantly of the Queen of Sheba (1 Kings 10:1-13; 2 Chronicles 9:1-12), Queen Vashti and Queen Esther (Esther 1:9-18, 2:22, 5:2-12, 7:1-8, 8:1, 9:12, 9:31), and figuratively of queens in Song of Songs 6:8-9. All 35 occurrences share this single lexical meaning across singular definite (הַמַּלְכָּה 'the queen'), construct (מַלְכַּת 'queen of'), and plural (מְלָכוֹת 'queens') forms. Multilingual evidence is uniform: Arabic الْمَلِكَة (al-malikah), Spanish 'reina', Hindi रानी (raani) / रानियाँ (raaniyaan, plural), Korean 왕비/여왕 (wangbi/yeowang), Swahili 'malkia'. The grammatical variation across definite, construct, and plural forms represents inflection, not distinct senses.
